# Terms of Art {#sec-appendix-terms-of-art}

The chapters introduce a small vocabulary of their own. Each entry below restates the owning chapter's definition in one line so that a reader who meets the term later in the book can find where it was earned (@tbl-glossary-terms).

| **Term** | **Definition** | **Defined in** |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Architecture result** | A supported comparison or finding whose assumptions, conditions, checks, alternatives, and limits are clear enough to inform the next design action. A valid result can reject every candidate or retain the reference design. | @sec-moonshot |
| **AI-native design system** | The complete technical capability that couples learned components with version-controlled project state, deterministic simulators, electronic design automation (EDA) toolchains, and formal verification engines under human commitment authority. The book's object of study; never called "AI-assisted". | @sec-moonshot |
| **Point AI assistance** | Use of a learned model or generative tool to accelerate one isolated task inside an established workflow, leaving the surrounding workflow unchanged. The only tier the book calls "AI-assisted". | @sec-moonshot |
| **Layer 1, Layer 2, Layer 3** | The three operational layers of AI in design work. Layer 1 accelerates isolated drafting and analysis tasks within an established workflow (point AI assistance). Layer 2 runs closed-loop search within a fixed, pre-bounded architectural container and cannot move an interface. Layer 3 structures the complete design stack around multi-tool closed-loop search, machine-usable intermediate representations, and rejectable verification harnesses (the AI-native design system). | @sec-moonshot |
| **Commitment authority** | The organizational decision threshold at which a designated human holds exclusive, nondelegable approval rights to advance an architectural recommendation across a consequential transition, so that automated generators never commit silicon capital or modify baseline contracts out of order. | @sec-moonshot |
| **Design loop** | The iterative cycle through which architects formulate intent, generate candidates, evaluate them with multi-fidelity simulators and EDA tools, interpret feedback, and refine choices toward a supported decision. It closes into a loop only when returned evidence changes the represented design state and triggers another allowed action. | @sec-design-loop-no-longer-scales |
| **Design path** | A sequence that runs the design-loop activities once, or that returns evidence which changes nothing in the represented state. A fixed, predeclared sweep is a design path, not a design loop. | @sec-design-loop-no-longer-scales |
| **Scoped study** | The application of the complete set of life-cycle responsibilities to one specific architecture question and one intended decision. | @sec-architecture-20-ontology |
| **Study record** | The record that preserves a scoped study's core question, attempts, observations, conclusions, and unresolved issues so another architect can inspect the work. Distinct from the per-run execution record. | @sec-architecture-20-ontology |
| **Design-Loop Card** | A standardized index that binds automated tool execution to human design intent, qualified evidence, and explicit approval rights; the card indexes the study record. | @sec-architecture-20-ontology |
| **Execution record** | The immutable structured record produced by every tool invocation, joining the authorized request, scheduler job, input parameters, execution status, returned artifacts, computational cost, and terminal failure cause, and pairing candidate identity with environment state, tool versions, and container digests. | @sec-architecture-20-ontology; @sec-architecture-environments-tool-interfaces |

: **Terms of art introduced by this book.** Each definition restates the owning chapter's definition sentence; the right-hand column points to the chapter that earns the term. {#tbl-glossary-terms tbl-colwidths="[18,62,20]"}
